newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks take surprise dive eyeing Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks take surprise dive eyeing Wall St.

text.p: Madrid stocks fell sharply on Friday, tracking a dive on Wall Street amid a futures expiry and taking the market by surprise, dealers said.
However the indices closed off lows, which neared four percent at one point, and concerns were not about medium term upside potential but rather volatility during the summer.
The general index fell 15.03 points, 2.43 percent, to 603.29 and the Ibex shed 188.60 points, 2.68 percent, to 6,846.18.
The Ibex is seen trading between 6,700 and 7,200 for rest of summer, with erratic movements expected.
The effect of increased volatility amid the futures expiry, and news this week that key international brokerages were downgrading their weighting in Spain pressured the market lower.
But dealers agreed prospects further out remained rosy.
"We could still see further correction later in the summer, but it won't fall further than this. Medium term the prospects are good and fund managers have to buy," said a Banesto trader.
Focus next week will turn to results from banks Santander and BBV next week, dealers said.
